title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

errors: Step (i), Y' ≪̸ Z, is justified only by 'Y ≪̸ Z, Y' ⊴ Y'. This requires ≪ to be monotone in the direction 'Y' ≪ Z and Y' ⊴ Y ⇒ Y ≪ Z'. If ⊴ is read as 'sub-figure', that is the wrong direction. Grothendieck's own hesitation (striking, then restoring the sentence) suggests he saw the problem. An alternative fix: transitivity X °≪ Y' ≪ Z ⇒ X ≪ Z, contradicting X |∘| Z. That argument is not written.
The equivalence 'Y' |∘| Z i.e. Y' ≠ Z' is asserted without justification. It presumably uses Y' ⊴ Y, Y |∘| Z, and compatibility within the préfigure, but the reasoning is not given.
The final question (is Σ_{A'} → Σ_A an embedding?) is left open.

ideas.what: Sub-ateliers defined by the condition Sousat (convexity of A' with respect to the composite relation °≪ followed by ◁)
ideas.modern_name: Convex / interval-closed substructure of an incidence or mereotopological structure; analogous to full subcomplexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart (general incidence geometry and mereotopology: Whitehead, Clarke, RCC)

ideas.what: Strict residual atelier {X | X ∥ S}, closed under ≪ and hence a sub-atelier
ideas.modern_name: Analogue of a residue or link-type subcomplex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Residues in buildings: Tits; links in complexes: classical

ideas.what: Broad residual atelier {X | X |∘| 𝔓, X ≪̸ 𝔓} for a préfigure 𝔓 is a sub-atelier, although non-V°(S) in general is not
ideas.modern_name: Roughly the complement of a closed star / link-type construction in point-free geometry

ideas.what: Question whether a sub-atelier inclusion induces an embedding of the 'sommet' completions Σ_{A'} ↪ Σ_A
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality and injectivity of a lattice / Boolean-type completion along substructure inclusions

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether inclusion of a sub-atelier induces an embedding Σ_{A'} ↪ Σ_A of the associated 'sommet' structures. The question is not settled here.
missed.quote: Dans ces genres cas, il faudrait vérifier si Σ_{A'} ↪ Σ_A ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the basic functoriality test for any theory of morphisms of ateliers. It is of minor interest unless the ateliers framework, a point-free theory of figures close to mereotopology, is revived.

missed.claim: Ateliers, with relations for part-of, incidence and disjointness and with sub-structures and residual sub-ateliers, form an unpublished Grothendieck version of point-free / mereotopological geometry. The later literature (e.g. RCC, contact algebras) does not mention it.
missed.quote: considérons "l'atelier résiduel strict" formé des X ∈ A telles que X ∥ S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest and could be compared with contact algebras or the Region Connection Calculus. The page itself contains only routine verifications.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine verifications that specific subsets satisfy the sub-atelier axiom, plus one open functoriality question. The framework itself is unpublished and of historical interest, but this page adds no substantive result.
transcription_corrections: 'il est [-stable-] {+formé+} pour ≪' should read 'fermé' (closed) for ≪, not 'formé'.
'S = 𝒫 est une partie {+fermée+}' should read 'S = 𝔓 est une préfigure' (Fraktur P, with an inserted accent), not 'partie fermée'.

In the struck line 'La relation Y'≪̸Z claire car Y≪̸Z', the dashed underline appears to be a stet mark restoring the text. The inserted 'Y'⊴Y.' belongs after 'Y≪̸Z', so the line reads: 'claire car Y ≪̸ Z, Y' ⊴ Y'.
'en effet, soit X °≪ Y' ⊴ Y': 'soit' is written 'sat' ('soit').
